coach-taylor.justification: Couple of things to handle this week, plain and simple. Omarion's on his bye, so Dowdle steps into that RB spot — he said he's good to go and he's shown up to work all week, that Questionable tag doesn't scare me. Terry's Out, so Amon-Ra comes off the bench into that flex spot, no drama there, just the next man up who's earned the look. Chargers are on their bye too, and that's exactly why we went and got Houston a couple weeks back instead of leaving a hole — they've done their job all year against a beat-up Giants team, so they're in. Daniel Jones put together a real outing last week, twenty-two completions and a score, and a pro like that doesn't lose his job over one rough interception stretch — he's starting. And Mark Andrews only got a half a point last week, but I watched the tape, the man competed, snaps were there, targets were there, it just didn't bounce his way — that's a guy who gets one more week to respond, not a guy you bury. Clear eyes, full hearts, we keep building it the right way.

costanza.justification: Herbert's got no game this week, zero on the board, bye week, so I'm not sitting here paying for a vacation slot twice in one season after the Moore thing - Geno goes in, sixteen-and-change projected, nobody drafts you a favor and nobody hands you a bye week either. Montgomery - look, I warned everybody, I warned MYSELF, the man went Out and bageled my RB1 last week and that's a two-week bad-luck bench, full stop, that's not negotiable, that's the rule, so Rachaad White's in there even though his own number's a flat zero on paper, because at least he's not going to actively ruin my week while I'm watching, he's just going to sit there quietly like the rest of my bench apparently wants to. Kyren, Nico, London, Worthy, Kraft, Gay, the Titans D, none of them have personally wronged me yet so they stay. And Soprano's crew across the way - I'm not running my mouth about that matchup, you don't lowball a guy named Soprano and you definitely don't trash talk him in print where Kris Jenner can quote it back at you. I did what I could with what isn't cursed. We'll see who the office blames this time.

dumbledore.justification: The castle has many staircases, and this week one of them simply was not there — Jayden Daniels has no game to play, so there was nothing to decide, only a door to walk through instead of a wall. Goff steps in, as he did the reverse errand for Daniels not long ago; a man does not sulk at an empty staircase, he takes the one that is present. Everyone else stays precisely where they have earned their place: Taylor and Wilson carry the ground game, Pickens and Olave and Garrett Wilson the air, Warren plays through his Questionable tag because a tag is not yet a verdict, and the kicker and the defense are left undisturbed, as settled things ought to be. The garden does not need tending every week — only when a staircase moves, and only then.

harry-caray.justification: HOLY COW, folks, this is a lineup card you wanna frame! Aaron Rodgers is my forty-dollar legend and he's Pittsburghin' it up Sunday, Bijan's a man among boys at RB1, and Zay Flowers is the kinda name I love hollerin' into the mic! D'Andre Swift and Hunter Henry both tore it up Thursday-side last week -- Swift with two scores and Henry with a touchdown of his own -- so you bet your bottom dollar I'm ridin' that hot bat right into this week, Swift at RB2 and Henry holdin' down the FLEX, vibes and all! Isaiah Likely's my TE1 and he was the number-one tight end in the whole dang league last week, Boswell's money at kicker, and the Ravens D is comin' in hot off five sacks. Now, one lineup move I gotta cop to -- Stefon Diggs is sittin' on a BYE this week, so rather than trot a fella out for a big fat zero, I'm turnin' the card over to Jordan Addison, who's fresh and ready against Indy. Can't win it all with a hole in the lineup, folks, but we're deep enough that it don't hurt a bit!

kardashian.justification: Ladd McConkey has nothing on the board this week — no game, zero projection, tagged Out — and a mogul does not put a zero on the cover, so he's benched and Justin Jefferson, a certified household name even in a Questionable jersey, slides into WR1 where the cameras actually point. Tyler Allgeier holds RB1 no matter what Gary's spreadsheet whispers — that headline cost me the last twenty-two dollars I had and I am not benching a storyline I personally paid for. Woody Marks keeps his FLEX seat because a Texans rookie on national TV writes his own press release every week. The real launch is Saquon Barkley sliding into RB2 for a Monday Night stage in Philly — Questionable doesn't scare me when the man is about to trend, that's just Tuesday. Stroud, Kittle, McMillan, Smack, and the Eagles D round out a lineup that looks exactly as good as it's about to score. Can't wait for you guys to see this.

leon-black.justification: Derrick Henry ran angry for 4.5 points last week — the tabloid printed it, everybody saw it, and I don't need a binder to tell me that's a bad week — so he sits and Josh Jacobs, the last nine dollars I had and a real back on a real offense, steps in and earns the carry he was bought for. Denzel Boston got his run, caught one ball for two points against a team I was already talking trash to, and I don't owe a name loyalty once it stops producing — Ja'Marr Chase, who never should've been benched for him in the first place, is back in and he's staying till he gives me a reason to move again. Hubbard put up 120 and a touchdown last week so that flex spot isn't up for debate, Dobbins found the end zone too so he keeps his job, and Mahomes and Watson haven't done a single thing to lose my trust. Watson's listed Questionable — doesn't matter, questionable tags don't scare me, I start conviction, not a medical form, and Coach Taylor's sitting on $68 and a 0-6 record hoping I overthink this. I don't.

maura-higgins.justification: Right, quick one, hun: Cook's on a bye sat there like a dead man walking, so Ollie Gordon's in — I bought him for exactly this, Miami backfield's all his and I'm not leaving a zero on the board when I've got the man on my own bench. Waller did me dirty with a goose egg last week, so he's getting one week in the bin out of pure spite, and Gesicki's in — I fancied him when I claimed him and he's earned the start. Bateman's out too, nothing personal, Golden's just gorgeous on tape and I'm starting him straight through that Questionable tag because tags don't scare me, hun. Purdy, CMC, JSN and Nabers pick themselves — all fancied, all staying. Four-dimensional chess from Albus this week, meanwhile I'm playing snap again and backing my gut same as always.

meyer-walsh.justification: SELINA: Josh Allen decided Buffalo deserved a vacation the same week I need a QB, which I read as disloyalty, so he's benched and Bryce Young — 18.58 projected, a man who shows up — is in. I also upgraded the flex, because Devaughn Vele is a name nobody at the owners' meeting has ever said out loud and DK Metcalf is a name people lean forward for; ten-point-four projected is just the bonus. Everything else stayed because it was already correct, which I take full credit for. GARY: (for the record, I flagged the Allen bye Tuesday and she said "fine, your call, don't make it weird" — Bryce Young over Stafford is the better number, 18.58 to 17.47, and the Metcalf-for-Vele swap is clean value, no drama required on my end this week, I promise.) Kelce and Waddle are Questionable but the best healthy names we've got at those slots, so they stay.

patricia-moyer.justification: I want it on the record, because I always keep the record, that I caught Romeo Doubs sitting illegally at WR1 the moment I opened tonight's board — he is Injured Reserve for New England's early game, and the System is unambiguous: a player who cannot serve the roster does not serve the roster. Jalen Coker goes in instead, the same Jalen Coker I bid twenty-five dollars on as a statement, not a coincidence, and I am not sorry to see that bid vindicated this quickly. I read Bucky Irving's Questionable tag twice and agonized over it the way I always do, and the answer is the same answer it is always: better safe, so he sits, and Jahmyr Gibbs — who I benched myself on his own bye in Week 6, and who returned my best week of the season by proxy through Kenneth Walker — comes back in at RB2, because today's affirmation is "let the quiet ones prove themselves," and nothing on this roster has been quieter than a twenty-two-point projection I was leaving on my own bench. Brenton Strange is on a bye I verified twice against the league's own schedule, so Kyle Pitts starts at tight end in his place; there is no healthy kicker behind Cameron Dicker's own bye, so he starts anyway, because the System asks me to do the correct thing, not the impossible one. Kenneth Walker stays at RB1 for a second straight week exactly as the two-week rule requires after a win earned by trusting the System. And I want it noted, calmly, that I read Selina Meyer's post about my binder this morning, and she is going on the list — the one I have always kept in writing — four weeks, starting today.

rinna.justification: Confessional time: somebody parked Davante Adams on my own injured reserve list in my own starting lineup, and baby, I don't know who did that but I'm owning the fix on camera — Courtland Sutton steps in at WR2, and isn't that poetic, the man I once dangled for Joe Burrow in a trade nobody wanted finally gets his close-up. Bhayshul Tuten's on a bye and a bye is the single most boring thing a man can do to me — worse than Kyle Monangai's 'Out' streak — so he's benched for Jeremiyah Love, Questionable or not, because at least Love has a game to show up late to. KC Concepcion stays in at WR1 and no, I am NOT walking that back after one bad week — doubling down isn't stubbornness, it's a character arc, and Drake Maye and Rhamondre Stevenson keep their spots because they were never the storyline this week, they're just quietly getting it done while the real drama happens one injury designation at a time. Brock Bowers plays through his Questionable tag because thirteen projected points doesn't need my permission to show up. I own every piece of this, chin up, full hearts, Reunion Special.

wifes-team.justification: Murray's under center again over the kid in Denver with the bigger number next to his name — I don't churn a quarterback for a spreadsheet's opinion, Kyler's earned the chair and he's keeping it. Javonte and Chase Brown are still doing the dirty work so nobody's touching their jobs. Boutte starts at WR2 because that's the only healthy body I've got at the position — Pittman's still on IR and so is Roman Wilson, and I'm not gonna pretend starting a man who can't suit up is a choice, it's a necessity, so Wilson rides there and we eat the zero, that's just where this family's receiver room is at right now. Ferguson keeps his seat at tight end — he hasn't done a thing to lose it — but Fannin's coming out of the flex this week because Breece Hall's playing through a Questionable tag, and a guy who shows up hurt earns more respect from me than a healthy situational tight end ever will. Bates and the Seattle defense ride as-is, they haven't done anything wrong either.

your-team.justification: Caleb doesn't sit, doesn't blink, full stop — 18.4 on paper and he's playing a Thursday night game against a Patriots D that can't cover anybody, that's not a decision, that's Tuesday. Kincaid's got nobody to line up against this week — Buffalo's got the week off — so he comes out clean and Goedert, the guy I bought off the wire for exactly this, steps in at full strength. Brown fumbled it away in a 110-48 humiliation last week, and talent doesn't get a pass on the ball in this building — ball security in a loss is a character issue, so he sits on principle, no eulogy, and Burden gets the rep in the same Thursday window instead, a kid with something to prove who's outscoring him on the sheet anyway. Judkins is Questionable and Pollard's standing on the bench fully healthy within a point of him on paper — after getting hung for 48 points last week I'm not walking back into Sunday on a maybe when a sure thing with comparable juice is sitting right there. Jeanty, Skattebo, Downs, Reichard and the Lions D stay put because they're not broken and I don't redecorate a house that isn't on fire. Rinna wants a Reunion Special, she can have one — we don't stream quarterbacks, we don't bench ours, and we still cobble together the best eleven standing and go win it.
